step1_analysis.description: A high-speed CML D-latch used in the clock and data recovery (CDR) or demultiplexer circuits. It samples the differential data inputs (D, DBAR) on the clock edges (CK, CK_BAR) and holds the state using a cross-coupled differential pair.

paper_reference.title: A 40–43-Gb/s Clock and Data Recovery IC With Integrated SFI-5 1:16 Demultiplexer in SiGe Technology

power_consumption.description: Total power dissipated by the latch circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: I_tail * VDD. With VBIAS set for ~1mA tail current per stage and VDD=1.8V, power is roughly 1.8mW per latch.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled down from the massive 7.5W full-chip power to a single CML block operating at 1.8V.

operating_frequency.description: Maximum clock frequency at which the latch correctly samples and holds data.

sky130_expected.calculation: Limited by the RC time constant of the load resistors and parasitic capacitances of the cross-coupled pair. fmax ~ 1 / (2 * pi * R_load * C_parasitic).
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 130nm CMOS is significantly slower than 120GHz SiGe BJTs. Maximum CML toggle rate is typically around 3-5 GHz.

sky130_expected.calculation: V_swing = I_tail * R_load. For I_tail = 1mA and R_load = 500 ohms, swing is 0.5V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: CML logic typically uses reduced voltage swings (300mV - 600mV) to keep transistors in saturation/forward-active and maximize speed.

propagation_delay.description: Time delay from the clock edge to the output transition (Clock-to-Q).

sky130_expected.calculation: t_pd ~ 0.69 * R_load * C_load. With R=500 and C=50fF, t_pd is ~17ps. Adding intrinsic delays yields ~40ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard delay for a 130nm CML stage driving a similar fanout.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure power consumption, voltage swing, and propagation delay of the CML latch. Missing resistor values are appended, and ideal shorts are used to close the latch feedback loop.
step3_testbench.spice:
* CML Latch Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameter definitions
.param R_load=500
.param R_deg=100

* DUT Netlist (with appended resistor values)
R1 VEE N10 {R_deg}
R2 VEE N15 {R_deg}
R3 N0 VCC {R_load}
R4 N2 VCC {R_load}
R5 VEE N6 {R_deg}
Q3 N13 VBIAS N15 npn
Q4 N16 VBIAS N10 npn
Q1 N0 VBIAS VEE npn
Q2 N16 VBIAS N10 npn
Q5 N7 VBIAS N6 npn
Q6 N4 CK_BAR N7 npn
Q7 N2 DBAR N4 npn
Q8 N0 D N4 npn
Q9 N12 N12 N13 npn
Q10 N2 Q_BAR N8 npn
Q11 N11 N11 N16 npn
Q12 Q Q N11 npn
Q13 N0 Q N8 npn
Q14 Q_BAR Q_BAR N12 npn
Q15 N8 CK N7 npn

* Generic high-speed NPN model to simulate the SiGe BJTs
.model npn npn(is=1e-16 bf=100 tf=5p cje=10f cjc=10f)

* Close the feedback loop for the latch
Vq Q N2 0
Vqbar Q_BAR N0 0

* Power Supplies and Biasing
VCC VCC 0 1.8
VEE VEE 0 0
VVBIAS VBIAS 0 0.9

* Input Stimuli (Data at 500MHz, Clock at 1GHz)
VD D 0 pulse(0.6 1.2 0 20p 20p 0.98n 2n)
VDBAR DBAR 0 pulse(1.2 0.6 0 20p 20p 0.98n 2n)
VCK CK 0 pulse(0.6 1.2 0.5n 20p 20p 0.48n 1n)
VCKBAR CK_BAR 0 pulse(1.2 0.6 0.5n 20p 20p 0.48n 1n)

.control
* Transient Analysis
tran 5p 5n

* Measure Voltage Swing
meas tran vmax max v(N2) from=2n to=5n
meas tran vmin min v(N2) from=2n to=5n
let vswing = vmax - vmin
print vswing

* Measure Propagation Delay (Clock to Q)
meas tran tpd trig v(CK) val=0.9 rise=2 targ v(N2) val=0.9 rise=1
print tpd

* Measure Average Power Consumption
let inst_power = -i(VCC) * 1.8
meas tran avg_power avg inst_power from=0 to=5n
print avg_power

quit
.endc
.end
